messages:
priya.kumar: Hey team - BrightLens reported a sudden rise of 502/504 responses from the hosted API around 2025-11-12 09:14 PST. They say ~3% of their /v1/generate calls fail, mostly when sending large single-request prompts (~1.2MB-2MB). They included a few request ids: rq_01F9X1A3, rq_01F9X1E7, rq_01F9X1M2. They can reproduce by issuing a single large POST with base64 payload. App is in production and customers notice degradation.

support-bot: Forwarding to oncall + SRE. @sre-bot which gateway are they hitting (edge nginx vs edge-proxy envoy)? Also any client retries configured?

priya.kumar: They're on hosted via edge-proxy (envoy). No client-side retry on their SDK. Example request they used:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"'"$(head -c 1500000 /dev/urandom | base64)"'"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sre-bot: Paged @jamal.ortega. Collected the proxy logs for the IDs above.

jamal.ortega: Pulling logs/traces now. Early observations from envoy on cluster-3:

```
[2025-11-12T09:14:21.123Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2" 504 - upstream request timeout, took 30.001s, response_flags = UT
[2025-11-12T09:14:21.124Z] envoy gc: stream id 45 reset, error: REFUSED_STREAM
[2025-11-12T09:14:21.125Z] cluster runtime-3: no healthy endpoints for host runtime-03
[2025-11-12T09:14:21.126Z] upstream reset: connection failure, reset reason: connection termination
```

jamal.ortega: From runtime-side metrics, large prompts (over ~800KB) spike tail latency due to kv-cache misses and fallback to slower kernels/alloc paths. When several such requests overlap we see upstream connection pool exhaustion. Envoy reports many REFUSED_STREAM and then 504/502 for the client.

alicia.park: Are we seeing this correlated with HTTP/2 multiplexing limits per connection? Might be head-of-line blocking when streams pile up.

jamal.ortega: Exactly. Concurrent streams per upstream connection for this customer jumped to ~18 from a baseline of 2-4. Runtime keepalive/concurrency caps were reached, new streams got REFUSED_STREAM or caused connection resets -> gateway errors.

dev.shah: I reproduced locally against staging with the following script:

```
# stress-large-prompts.sh
for i in {1..30}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"'"$(head -c 1200000 /dev/urandom | base64)"'"}' &
done
wait
```

dev.shah: Under that run envoys returned a mix of 504 and REFUSED_STREAM. Runtime OOM not observed but memory allocs + slow kernel fallback caused requests to hang near the 30s upstream timeout.

jamal.ortega: Short-term mitigations on the table:
- route BrightLens API key to a warm, dedicated runtime pool (pin their key) - quick route rule
- increase envoy http2 max_concurrent_streams and tweak http2 options in cluster config - quick canary roll
- add a gateway retry for 504s with jitter (risky for duplicate side-effects and cost)

priya.kumar: Customer explicitly asked no automatic retries to avoid duplicate bills. They prefer routing to dedicated warm pool if possible.

jamal.ortega: I'm standing up a canary to route the customer's key to warm-pool-2 and applying an envoy http2 tweak (canary) limited to affected edge-proxies. Deploying now.

[2025-11-12T09:19:02.881Z] deploy-bot: route-rule apply succeeded (canary: brightlens -> warm-pool-2)

alicia.park: Pushed an envoy canary bump to http2 options: max_concurrent_streams 64 (was 16) and bumped initial_stream_window_size. Config snippet:

```
cluster:
  name: runtime-cluster
  http2_options:
    max_concurrent_streams: 64
    initial_stream_window_size: 65536
```

alicia.park: Rolling to 10% of edge-proxies for now.

jamal.ortega: Monitoring metrics: error rate for BrightLens dropped from ~3.1% to 0.2% within about 40s of the canary changes. P95 latency improved from ~3.8s to ~1.2s for that customer's traffic (still above baseline due to large payloads but stable).

priya.kumar: BrightLens confirms errors stopped. They asked for an RCA and long-term fixes.

jamal.ortega: Preliminary RCA: heavy single-request payloads (1MB+) cause KV cache misses and fallback slow paths in runtime, creating long-tail request durations. Combined with low http2 concurrency limits and insufficient connection pooling at the edge this led to upstream connection exhaustion, REFUSED_STREAMs, and resulting 502/504s.

dev.shah: Long-term proposals:
- add soft enforcement and clear 413 guidance for very large prompts (reject > 2MB with helpful message)
- improve runtime large-payload handling (cache warming, memory path optimizations, faster quantized kernel fallback)
- routing automation: auto-warm/pin heavy API keys to dedicated pools
- standardize envoy http2 defaults across clusters

alicia.park: I'll own the infra change to standardize http2 defaults (PR to infra repo). Jamal please track routing automation, and Dev can coordinate runtime optimizations.

jamal.ortega: Creating a ticket and a short postmortem doc. Draft link uploaded internally.

priya.kumar: Sending a customer-facing summary and action plan to BrightLens now. Closing thread as mitigated. Thanks all :heart:

[2025-11-12T09:26:45.002Z] priya.kumar uploaded: https://redwood.company/postmortems/2025-11-12-brightlens-edge-504s-draft (internal)

priya.kumar: Action items (brief):
- infra: standardize envoy http2 defaults (alicia) - due 2025-11-19
- routing: implement auto-warm routing for heavy keys (jamal) - due 2025-11-26
- runtime: evaluate prompt-size handling & optimize cache warming (dev) - due 2025-12-03

support-bot: Incident recorded as SUPPORT_ESCALATION. Postmortem link above. If BrightLens sees further issues reopen here.
